html:
Alberto Fujimori was the president of Peru from 1990 to 2000. The son of Japanese immigrants, he ended hyperinflation and saw the defeat of the Shining Path, but ruled as an autocrat and was later imprisoned.

An agronomist with no political career, he beat the novelist Mario Vargas Llosa in the 1990 election. He then imposed harsh economic shock measures that ended hyperinflation. In 1992 he shut Congress and the courts with the army's support. The capture of the Shining Path leader that year made him popular.

His spy chief bribed politicians and the press, and death squads killed civilians. In 2000, amid scandal, he fled to Japan and resigned by fax. Extradited from Chile, he was convicted in 2009 of human rights crimes. He was pardoned in 2023 and died in 2024. His daughter Keiko leads his political movement in Peru.
